scenes.tts: Can a growth cone with the same receptor turn toward netrin in one condition and away in another?
scenes.visual: Title card: Same Receptor, Opposite Turn. One growth cone with two ghost paths, one bending toward a source and one away. Question on screen.
scenes.narration: Can a growth cone with the same receptor turn toward netrin in one condition and away in another?

scenes.tts: Start on the map, then zoom into one growth cone in a dish.
scenes.visual: The transverse spinal cord map: dorsal commissural neurons at top, floor plate at the ventral midline, ventricular zone around the central canal, pial surface at the outer edge, commissural path drawn from dorsal cord down near the pia, then in across the floor plate. The view zooms from the map into a single growth cone in a culture dish.
scenes.narration: Start on the map, then zoom into one growth cone in a dish.

scenes.tts: Receptors are one layer. In some cells, the growth cone's internal state is a second.
scenes.visual: Two stacked layers on the growth cone: receptors on the surface, internal state inside.
scenes.narration: Receptors are one layer. In some cells, the growth cone's internal state is a second.

scenes.tts: Mu-ming Poo's laboratory developed a turning assay. A fine pipette puffs short, regular pulses of a cue beside one growth cone.
scenes.visual: A fine pipette off to one side of a growth cone releases regular puffs; a gradient forms across the growth cone.
scenes.narration: Mu-ming Poo's laboratory developed a turning assay. A fine pipette puffs short, regular pulses of a cue beside one growth cone.

scenes.tts: Time-lapse imaging measures which way the growth cone turns.
scenes.visual: Time-lapse frames stack up; an angle marker measures the turn.
scenes.narration: Time-lapse imaging measures which way the growth cone turns.

scenes.tts: In nineteen ninety-seven, Guo-li Ming and colleagues used frog spinal neurons. Their growth cones turned toward netrin one.
scenes.caption: In 1997, Guo-li Ming and colleagues used frog spinal neurons. Their growth cones turned toward netrin-1.
scenes.visual: Label: 1997, frog spinal neurons. The growth cone bends toward the pipette.
scenes.narration: In 1997, Guo-li Ming and colleagues used frog spinal neurons. Their growth cones turned toward netrin-1.

scenes.tts: Next they blocked cyclic A M P signalling. They blocked P K A, the enzyme cyclic A M P switches on.
scenes.caption: Next they blocked cAMP signalling. They blocked PKA, the enzyme cAMP switches on.
scenes.visual: Inside the growth cone, cAMP activates PKA; a block symbol appears over PKA.
scenes.narration: Next they blocked cAMP signalling. They blocked PKA, the enzyme cAMP switches on.

scenes.tts: With P K A blocked, they puffed netrin again. Toward, away, or no turn?
scenes.caption: With PKA blocked, they puffed netrin again. Toward, away, or no turn?
scenes.visual: The pipette puffs netrin beside the blocked growth cone. Three options on screen: toward, away, no turn.
scenes.narration: With PKA blocked, they puffed netrin again. Toward, away, or no turn?

scenes.tts: The same growth cones turned away. Attraction had become repulsion.
scenes.visual: The growth cone bends away from the pipette. Label: repulsion.
scenes.narration: The same growth cones turned away. Attraction had become repulsion.

scenes.tts: Now add an antibody to D C C. If the receptor stays the same, what should the antibody block?
scenes.caption: Now add an antibody to DCC. If the receptor stays the same, what should the antibody block?
scenes.visual: Antibodies cover the DCC receptors on the growth cone. Question on screen.
scenes.narration: Now add an antibody to DCC. If the receptor stays the same, what should the antibody block?

scenes.tts: It stopped both turns, the attraction and the repulsion. Both needed D C C.
scenes.caption: It stopped both turns, the attraction and the repulsion. Both needed DCC.
scenes.visual: Two panels, normal and PKA blocked; with anti-DCC both growth cones grow straight. Label: both turns need DCC.
scenes.narration: It stopped both turns, the attraction and the repulsion. Both needed DCC.

scenes.tts: The receptor was the same. The cell's cyclic A M P chose the direction, in this system.
scenes.caption: The receptor was the same. The cell's cAMP chose the direction, in this system.
scenes.visual: One DCC receptor with a switch inside the growth cone labelled cAMP, flipping the arrow.
scenes.narration: The receptor was the same. The cell's cAMP chose the direction, in this system.

scenes.tts: This is the rule's second limit at work. A growth cone carrying D C C was repelled.
scenes.caption: This is the rule's second limit at work. A growth cone carrying DCC was repelled.
scenes.visual: The rule card from chapter one; the limit 'receptors plus state' lights.
scenes.narration: This is the rule's second limit at work. A growth cone carrying DCC was repelled.

scenes.tts: It is one worked example in one system. It is not a rule for every netrin-responsive axon.
scenes.visual: A tag on the frog growth cone: one system. Other axons fade in, unlabelled.
scenes.narration: It is one worked example in one system. It is not a rule for every netrin-responsive axon.

scenes.tts: Calcium can also change the response.
scenes.visual: Calcium ions flicker inside the growth cone.
scenes.narration: Calcium can also change the response.

scenes.tts: So can laminin, and the eye shows why a flip might be useful. Retinal axons run along the inner surface of the retina to the exit.
scenes.visual: A retina in section; axons run along the inner surface toward the optic disk.
scenes.narration: So can laminin, and the eye shows why a flip might be useful. Retinal axons run along the inner surface of the retina to the exit.

scenes.tts: That exit is the optic disk, where netrin one is concentrated.
scenes.caption: That exit is the optic disk, where netrin-1 is concentrated.
scenes.visual: Netrin-1 concentrated at the optic disk. Label: optic disk (optic nerve head).
scenes.narration: That exit is the optic disk, where netrin-1 is concentrated.

scenes.tts: In mice lacking netrin one or D C C, the axons still reach the optic disk. But they fail to leave through it.
scenes.caption: In mice lacking netrin-1 or DCC, the axons still reach the optic disk. But they fail to leave through it.
scenes.visual: Mutant retina: axons pile up at the optic disk instead of leaving.
scenes.narration: In mice lacking netrin-1 or DCC, the axons still reach the optic disk. But they fail to leave through it.

scenes.tts: In frog retinal growth cones, laminin one lowers cyclic A M P. It turns netrin's attraction into repulsion.
scenes.caption: In frog retinal growth cones, laminin-1 lowers cAMP. It turns netrin's attraction into repulsion.
scenes.visual: A growth cone on a laminin-coated surface; cAMP falls and the turn flips to away.
scenes.narration: In frog retinal growth cones, laminin-1 lowers cAMP. It turns netrin's attraction into repulsion.

scenes.tts: Laminin lies on the retinal surface. In the authors' model, netrin repels where laminin and netrin overlap. That may help push axons down into the exit.
scenes.visual: Label: proposed model. The retinal surface coated with laminin; at the overlap with netrin, axons are pushed down into the optic disk, where there is netrin without laminin.
scenes.narration: Laminin lies on the retinal surface. In the authors' model, netrin repels where laminin and netrin overlap. That may help push axons down into the exit.

scenes.tts: The takeaway: the growth cone decides, with its receptors and, in some cells, its internal state.
scenes.visual: The transverse spinal cord map: dorsal commissural neurons at top, floor plate at the ventral midline, ventricular zone around the central canal, pial surface at the outer edge, commissural path drawn from dorsal cord down near the pia, then in across the floor plate. Takeaway on screen: receptors plus internal state.
scenes.narration: The takeaway: the growth cone decides, with its receptors and, in some cells, its internal state.
